summary: An 1885 wooden lighthouse on the north side of the Annapolis Basin, facing Goat Island; restored by its Port Royal volunteers in 2023.

light.note: Fixed white, year round (Coast Guard List of Lights, light 210). In 1885 the light was fixed white, 55 ft (about 17 m) above high water, visible 11 miles (Department report, as quoted by Lighthouse Friends).

lens.note: A small dioptric lens in 1885; current apparatus not stated in the sources read

structures.note: Square-tapered wooden tower with superimposed gallery and red octagonal iron lantern. Register gives 13 m (43 ft); Coast Guard list gives the tower 11.1 m.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Reached by Granville Road from Route 1 at Lower Granville, about 10 km; small parking area beside the lighthouse.

facts.agency: Port Royal Lighthouse Association (owner and steward since 2022); the light is listed by the Canadian Coast Guard
facts.ownership_note: Department of Fisheries and Oceans owned and maintained it until 2015; Annapolis Heritage Society owned it from 2015; Port Royal Lighthouse Association from September 2022.

events.note: Tower built by John Wagstaff of Annapolis under contract for $900
Stone retaining wall built in front of the tower against erosion
Jacob V. Roblee appointed in place of Healy, whose appointment had been cancelled
Entrance steps repaired, new lock fitted to the door, new lamp supplied
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse, 12 February 2015, under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act
From Department of Fisheries and Oceans to Annapolis Heritage Society
Reshingling revealed extensive wood rot in corner posts; the society did not go ahead with the repairs
Ownership acquired by the Port Royal Lighthouse Association, September 2022
Renovation from late July to early November 2023 by volunteers and contractors funded by local, Parks Canada and municipal sources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register (13 m, 43 ft) and the 1885 report (43 ft base to vane) agree on the whole height; the Coast Guard list gives the tower 11.1 m. The story reports both and does not resolve it.

Lighthouse Friends' keeper line (Healy 1885-1897; Roblee 1897-1912; Healy 1912 to at least 1923) matches the Department's keeper index, which lists Roblee at Shafner Point, appointed 29 May 1897 (checked on the page image). The index gives no years for Healy, so the Healy dates rest on Lighthouse Friends alone.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate station. The 1885 report is quoted only by Lighthouse Friends and the Port Royal Lighthouse Association; the 1885 volume is not in the local corpus (corpus starts 1900), so the description is second-hand. The 1897 investigation finding is second-hand too (Lighthouse Friends; not in the corpus). The Department's 1906 keeper index (n4) shows 'Roblee, Jacob V  Shafner Point  May 29, 1897 150 00' on printed page 174 (scan 183); checked on the page image during fact-check 2026-10-27, so the 1897 appointment is confirmed by the Department as well as by Lighthouse Friends. Healy's 1912 return is Lighthouse Friends only: the 1912 to 1915 tables list 'J. K. Healy' but in column order without a station, so they were not used. Lloyd Shafner (Port Royal Lighthouse Association) is not in the Department's tables read and has no dates; he is listed without years and his place in the sequence is unknown. Check whether Shafner was a keeper after Healy in the 1920s: the corpus ends in 1924. Name spelling varies: Schafner, Shafner, Shaffner, Schaffner, Robblee and Roblee. Same-name trap: the 1908 notice on the removal of the schooner Ida M. Shaffner is at Port Bickerton, not here; the 1914 keeper list names 'Schaffner' with no station. Neither is used. Storms, wrecks and rescues: no wreck or rescue tied to this station was found in the corpus or on the pages read, so that chapter is omitted. Distance from the Habitation: Lighthouse Friends says 1 km beyond it on the drive in; the Association says less than 1 km from the Parks Canada Habitation; the story gives both. The $89,000 repair estimate is in Lighthouse Friends only (the Association's page does not give it), so it is footnoted to Lighthouse Friends alone. Ownership is stated consistently by Lighthouse Friends and the Association (federal to 2015, Annapolis Heritage Society 2015, Port Royal Lighthouse Association 2022); the record's agency and ownership fields match. Photos: the Heritage Guide copy credits a Wikimedia Commons photo (Dennis G. Jarvis, CC BY-SA 2.0) that is not added here; the Commons file URL was not read. Wikipedia's article was read as a lead only and is not cited. Shape (fact-check 2026-10-27): the story has five chapters (The place, Building the light, The keepers, After the keepers, Today); the guide allows two to four for moderate evidence. Left as written for the editor to decide, since merging would rename chapters.
